candidates.hypothesis: August 2026 arrivals can be estimated by applying the year-over-year growth rate observed in recent months to the August 2025 actual figure. The most recent months (June, July 2026) provide the latest growth trend, while August 2025 provides the seasonal base.

The number of foreign nationals entering Japan in August 2026 can be approximated from MOJ's monthly immigration statistics, which may be published with a similar lag. candidates.hypothesis: Foreign visitor arrivals are a subset of total international passenger arrivals at Japanese airports and seaports. By estimating total international arrivals in August 2026 and applying the historical share of foreign visitors, we can derive the target. This route requires data on flight schedules, seat capacity, and load factors.

assessment.note: Both describe the same underlying phenomenon: a severe (~57%) year-on-year decline in new entrants from mainland China in early 2026. p1 is the April monthly figure; p2 is the Jan–Apr cumulative figure. They are not independent (same source, same measurement), but they consistently indicate a deep, persistent collapse in Chinese arrivals rather than a one-month anomaly.

p3 gives the level of study-related new entrants from China in Jan–Feb 2026 (390 people); p4 gives the approximate year-on-year decline (~30%). They are consistent with each other and with the broader China weakness in p1/p2, though they cover a much narrower visa category (study) and a different period.

These are four market-level booking growth rates from the same JAPANiCAN.com source for Jan–Apr 2026. They are not independent of each other (same platform, same period), but together they show a clear pattern: strong growth from Taiwan and South Korea, near-flat US, and weak China/Hong Kong. This pattern is consistent with the China weakness in p1/p2 and provides a directional signal for the source-market mix in August 2026.

Both are monthly all-room occupancy rates from the same MLIT source (Feb 2026: 59.6%; Mar 2026: 60.3%). They are not independent observations of the target, but they establish a recent, modestly rising occupancy baseline that can inform a capacity-utilisation route for August 2026.

p28 reports that 15 markets set record-high June 2026 arrivals. This is a broad, positive signal for inbound tourism in mid-2026, but it does not directly quantify August 2026 arrivals and is not a substitute for a level estimate.

decisions.reason: The value 2,026 is a calendar year (the year the 5th Tourism Nation Promotion Basic Plan was formulated), not a count, rate, or conversion factor. It is irrelevant to estimating August 2026 visitor arrivals.

extra_directions.hypothesis: JNTO's monthly estimate for August 2026 will be published in mid-September 2026. If a preliminary or leaked figure, or a closely related MOJ immigration count for August 2026, becomes available before the cutoff, it would directly anchor the target and eliminate the need for a forecast. This is the single most valuable missing input.

extra_directions.hypothesis: A reliable August seasonal factor (August arrivals divided by the annual monthly average) for recent years would allow an annual 2026 forecast to be converted into an August 2026 level. Without this factor, any annual forecast cannot be transferred to the target month.
extra_directions.data_to_find: JNTO monthly arrivals for August and annual totals for 2023, 2024, and 2025, or a published seasonal index for Japan inbound tourism.

assumptions.rationale: No kept point directly gives August 2026 arrivals or a 2026 annual forecast. The JAPANiCAN booking growth (p5–p8) shows strong Taiwan/Korea growth but weak China/Hong Kong, and p28 shows record June 2026 arrivals in many markets. These are mixed but net-positive signals. A wide range around 1.0 reflects the offsetting market trends and the absence of a direct 2026 level forecast.
assumptions.applies_when: Used to scale a known August 2025 JNTO arrivals level to August 2026. It transfers only if the source-market mix and macro conditions in August 2026 are broadly similar to those implied by the kept booking and record-arrival evidence.
assumptions.falsified_by: A published JNTO or MOJ figure for August 2026, or a credible 2026 annual forecast implying a growth rate outside the stated range.

methods.rationale: Scales an assumed August 2025 level (a1) by a ratio (a2) informed by early-2026 market trends: strong Taiwan/Korea bookings (p5, p6) offset by a severe China decline (p1, p2, p7). This route is simple but relies on an assumed August 2025 level and a wide uncertainty band. Failure mode: if August 2025 was not ~3.4 million or if the market mix shifts dramatically. Note: this method uses only assumptions, so it is not executable under the rules; it is retained only as a conceptual placeholder and will be replaced by a method using kept data points.

assumptions.name: August 2025 JNTO foreign visitor arrivals
assumptions.rationale: August is a peak month; recent JNTO monthly totals have been in the 3–3.5 million range. No kept point supplies the August 2025 level directly, so this is an assumption. The range reflects uncertainty about the exact 2025 peak level.
assumptions.applies_when: Used as the base level for scaling to August 2026; assumes August 2025 was a typical recent peak month.
assumptions.falsified_by: A published JNTO figure for August 2025 outside 3.0–3.8 million.

assumptions.name: August 2026 foreign visitor arrivals relative to August 2025
assumptions.rationale: Early-2026 evidence shows strong Taiwan/Korea booking growth (p5, p6) but a severe China contraction (p1, p2, p7). China is a large source market, so the net effect on total arrivals is highly uncertain. A central ratio of 1.0 with a wide range reflects offsetting market trends and the absence of a clear aggregate signal.
assumptions.applies_when: Used to scale August 2025 JNTO arrivals to August 2026; assumes the market mix and policy environment in August 2026 are broadly similar to early 2026 with no major new shocks.
assumptions.falsified_by: Evidence of a large new visa policy, travel advisory, or economic shock affecting Japan inbound travel in mid-2026, or a published JNTO/MOJ figure for August 2026 showing a change outside the range.

methods.label: m1
methods.rationale: Scales an assumed August 2025 level (a1) by a ratio (a2) informed by early-2026 market trends: strong Taiwan/Korea bookings (p5, p6) offset by a severe China decline (p1, p2, p7). This route is simple but relies on an assumed August 2025 level and a wide uncertainty band. Failure mode: if August 2025 was not ~3.4 million or if the market mix shifts dramatically. Note: this method uses only assumpt
methods.error: input a1: assumption a1 was rejected (target-like: a level of the target quantity (unit or name matches the target, no ratio wording))

kept.applies_when: Used to scale August 2025 JNTO arrivals to August 2026; assumes the market mix and policy environment in August 2026 are broadly similar to early 2026 with no major new shocks.

by_construction: Only URLs leave the searcher (code regex); extractor, judge and final prompts never contain search result titles, snippets or the searcher's text. This holds by construction and is not measured.
residual_risks: The searcher sees post-cutoff search results and chooses which URLs are fetched, so page selection can be conditioned on the answer; only the URLs leave the searcher, and in backtests every fetched page is a snapshot dated <= as_of.
Live pages are used only when as_of is today; in backtests every page is an archived snapshot dated <= as_of.
The leak sentinel only catches registered official values in common formats, not paraphrased or derived numbers.
The model's own training data (knowledge cutoff unpublished) can include history before as_of; it cannot include the target if the target was published after the model's release.
Wayback snapshots are captured by a third party; a snapshot date <= as_of proves the content existed by then.
Assumption values are proposed by the judge model from its own knowledge, which can include the target's history before as_of; code checks their form, not where the number came from.

ablation.rule: exclude points from own_history directions and points whose name contains a target entity anchor and whose name or unit shares a stem with the target unit (triangulate/agent/ablation.py)
residual_risks: Own values named by an alias or abbreviation, or with no entity in the point name, are not excluded.

The rule over-excludes on purpose: any point naming the target entity together with the target quantity (for example a survey of the target's visitors) is excluded, even when it is not a value of the target itself.
The model's own memory of the target's history is not removed: it can still shape the plan, the judge's choices and assumption values.
The searcher and the extractor still see pages that contain own values; only the judge's table is filtered.
